title: tariff-spec-extraction
description: One (provider x utility schedule) rate layer, transcribed from a pdftotext -layout rendering of that layer's published rate sheet. Every numeric value carries a verbatim span from the source that the driver re-greps. This object is NOT the repo's spec YAML: the driver converts it. `evidence` is checked and then dropped.

schedule_id.description: The UTILITY's own schedule identifier, exactly as the source prints it: TOU-DR1, E-TOU-C, EV-TOU-5. Transcribe it; never coin one. Do NOT namespace it with the supplier (not MCE-E-TOU-C). The supplier goes in `provider`.

name.description: Human-readable name for this layer, e.g. 'Clean Energy Alliance generation (Clean Impact) matched to SDG&E TOU-DR1'.

provider.description: Who supplies this layer: the CCA's short name (CEA, SDCP, MCE, 3CE) for a generation layer, or the utility (SDG&E, PG&E) for a delivery layer or utility-bundled generation.

layer.description: delivery = the utility's UDC + non-bypassable charges. generation = the commodity, whether utility-bundled or from a CCA.

effective_date.description: The date the sheet states these rates take effect, ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Use the sheet's own effective date, never the retrieval date and never today.

month_to_season.description: Every calendar month mapped to its season. Twelve independent decisions, each diffable against the sheet. This shape exists so that a month in NEITHER season (which raises only at bill time) and a month in BOTH (which silently prices as summer, forever) are both unrepresentable.

season_evidence.description: The span stating the season boundaries, e.g. 'Summer - June through September; Winter - October through May'.

tou.description: Time-of-use periods as ORDERED, first-match-wins rules plus a default for every hour no rule claims. Do not write a rule for the default period; that is what `default_period` is for.

hours.description: Half-open local-clock windows [start, end). 4pm-9pm is [16, 21]. A window may not wrap midnight — split it into two.

days.description: 'weekend' means the schedule's weekend/holiday table: Sat, Sun and the named calendar's observed holidays.

months.description: Only if the sheet restricts this window to certain months, e.g. SDG&E's 10am-2pm super-off-peak 'in March and April'. Omit otherwise.

default_period.description: The period every unclaimed hour falls into — normally off_peak.

holiday_calendar.description: Which utility's observed-holiday list moves a weekday onto the weekend table. Pick the calendar of the UTILITY whose meter this rides, even for a CCA layer. null means weekends only.

labels.description: period -> the bill-line label the sheet prints, e.g. {"super_off_peak": "Super Off-Peak"}.

tou_evidence.description: The span stating the TOU hours, e.g. 'SUMMER PEAK ... 5pm to 8pm, Monday - Friday'.

energy.description: Per-kWh energy rates, keyed by TOU period and then by season. BOTH seasons are required for every period: a missing winter column is the commonest transcription loss and this shape makes it impossible.

fixed_per_day.description: $/day standing charge (SDG&E 'Base Services Charge', PG&E 'Meter Charge'). null if this layer has none — generation layers normally do not.

fixed_name.description: The sheet's own name for the fixed charge, if it has one.

adders.description: Standing per-kWh line items that are not the energy rate: credits, exit fees, program charges. A per-kWh value may be NEGATIVE here — CEA's Rate Relief Credit is -0.03871 — so do not drop the sign.

per_kwh.description: A single season- and period-flat rate.

per_kwh_by_vintage.description: For the PCIA only: the year the customer's load left bundled service -> $/kWh. Transcribe the whole published column; the vintage is a customer fact supplied at bill time.

applies_to.description: 'cca' for lines only an unbundled customer pays (the vintaged PCIA). 'all' unless the sheet says otherwise.

components.description: Component name -> its rate. ZERO and NEGATIVE are legitimate and cited here and nowhere else (SDG&E prints Nuclear Decommissioning at 0.00000 and a Competition Transition Charge of -0.00007). Transcribe them as printed.

included_in_energy_rate.description: true when the components are already inside the energy rate above and are itemised only for reporting — which is how SDG&E prints them. false would double-charge them.

rate.description: A fraction, not a percent: 1.06% is 0.0106.

unverified.description: REQUIRED USE. Any field the source does not state, states ambiguously, or you could not locate. Naming it here is always correct and costs nothing; guessing it is the one unrecoverable error in this pipeline, because a plausible wrong rate passes every downstream check until it meets a real bill. Never fill a value from another document, from a sibling schedule, or from memory.

field.description: Dotted path into this object, e.g. 'energy.super_off_peak.winter'.

notes.description: Anything a human diffing this against the sheet should know: products deliberately not modeled, a line item you were unsure how to classify, a discrepancy inside the source. Prose, goes into the YAML header comment.

season.description: The season this month bills under, per the sheet's own boundaries.

periodName.description: snake_case TOU period key. Use the repo's vocabulary where it fits: on_peak, off_peak, super_off_peak, peak, offpeak. The same spelling must be used in `tou` and in `energy`.

citation.description: Prose provenance, in the style the repo's committed specs use: publisher, document title, the sheet's effective date, the named table or row the value came from, the URL, and the retrieval date. Specific enough that a reader can open the document and land on the number.

evidence.description: A machine-checkable pointer, distinct from `citation`. The driver asserts that `span` occurs VERBATIM in the source text and that the numbers you emitted occur inside it. A citation that is merely well-formed proves nothing; this is the first check in the pipeline that does not route through your own judgment.

span.description: Copied character-for-character from the source, including its internal spacing. Use the WHOLE -layout row, not the bare number: the row is what binds the value to its schedule, period and season column. Never reflow, re-space, summarise or correct it.

locator.description: Where in the document the span sits: the table name and row, plus a page or line number if the text carries one.

energyRate.description: One season x period energy cell. At least one of standard/care must be present: a cell with both absent loads cleanly and then raises at bill time, months later.

standard.description: $/kWh. Bounds are deliberately ~10x observed headroom; they catch a decimal shift, not a wrong-but-plausible rate. Transcribe every digit the sheet prints.

care.description: $/kWh for the CARE class. Only if the sheet PRINTS one. If the sheet says a CCA bills one rate regardless of CARE status, set this equal to standard and say so in `notes`. Never derive it from a discount percentage.
